title: Expected Masked Walsh Character
statement: Let $S\subseteq[n]$, and choose $r$ uniformly from the Boolean cube $\{0,1\}^n$. If $M(r)=\{i:r_i=0\}$ and $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$, then $\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{S\subseteq M(r)}\chi_S(r)]=(1/2)^{|S|}$.
hypotheses_covered: Natural number $n$ defining the Boolean cube
replaced: For every $S\subseteq[n]$ and uniform $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $M(r)=\{i:r_i=0\}$ and $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$. Then $\mathbb E_r[\mathbf1_{S\subseteq M(r)}\chi_S(r)]=2^{-|S|}$.
